program.merge_policy: accumulate twenty 25-finding deep passes; consolidate and run heavy validation after Wave 2500

source_provenance: Direct PubMed/NCBI discovery and abstract verification
PMID-level dedupe against accepted ledger plus concurrent reserved PMID state

waves.title: Kava Withdrawal Treated With Phenobarbital-A Case Report and Literature Review.
waves.study: case report plus systematic review of 9 prior studies
waves.population: heavy escalating kava use; prior controlled low-dose cessation studies
waves.finding: A heavy kava user developed hyperactive-delirium withdrawal after escalating intake and required medically supervised phenobarbital/dexmedetomidine; controlled low-dose cessation studies generally reported no withdrawal.
waves.safety: Severe withdrawal appears rare but possible with heavy use; case-level treatment does not establish a standard self-management protocol.

waves.title: Efficacy of melatonin vs. midazolam for oral premedication in children: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Melatonin and midazolam did not significantly differ for sedation or anxiety before or during induction.
waves.safety: Dose and outcome heterogeneity were substantial; perioperative evidence is not ordinary pediatric sleep-supplement evidence.

waves.title: Research Review: Omega-3 supplementation to reduce antisocial behavior - a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.population: mixed populations with antisocial/externalizing behavior outcomes
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation produced a statistically significant but small reduction in antisocial behavior; pooled externalizing-behavior evidence was also modestly favorable.
waves.safety: Small effects and equivocal publication-bias evidence support adjunctive, not stand-alone, interpretation.

waves.title: Ginkgo biloba extract EGb 761 is safe and effective in the treatment of mild dementia - a meta-analysis of patient subgroups in randomised controlled trials.
waves.study: subgroup meta-analysis of 4 randomized placebo-controlled trials; 782 patients
waves.finding: Standardized EGb 761 improved cognition, global assessment, activities of daily living, and quality of life versus placebo in the selected subgroup.
waves.safety: Evidence applies to standardized EGb 761, not generic Ginkgo products; adverse-event frequency was similar to placebo.

waves.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of the acute effect of caffeine on attention.
waves.study: meta-analysis of 31 randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trials; 1,455 participants
waves.finding: Acute caffeine modestly improved attention reaction time and accuracy; reaction-time benefit rose with dose, while accuracy showed a nonlinear relationship.
waves.safety: Acute performance meta-regression does not define a universally safe or optimal dose.

waves.title: Beneficial Impacts of pre- and Postoperative Probiotics/Synbiotics Supplementation in Patients Undergoing Gastrointestinal Surgeries: An Umbrella Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Perioperative probiotics/synbiotics were associated with fewer infections and diarrhea, shorter hospital stay and antibiotic duration, and lower pooled mortality.
waves.safety: Heterogeneous surgeries, products, and protocols make this perioperative clinical-nutrition evidence, not routine consumer-use evidence.

waves.title: Probiotic Lactobacillus sp. as a strategy for modulation of non-comorbid obesity: A systematic meta-analysis and GRADE assessment of randomized controlled trials.
waves.study: systematic meta-analysis of 12 clinical trials; 1,058 participants
waves.population: people with obesity without major comorbidities
waves.finding: Lactobacillus-based probiotics produced small reductions in body weight, BMI, waist/hip circumference, and several adiposity measures, with favorable leptin/adiponectin changes.
waves.safety: Strain and intervention diversity limit generalization; effect sizes are modest.

waves.title: Effects of Probiotic Supplementation on Mental Health and the Risk of Depression in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
waves.finding: Small trials reported improvements in sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and selected PCOS-related quality-of-life domains.
waves.safety: Few studies, modest samples, and methodological variability make the evidence preliminary and product-dependent.

waves.title: [Therapeutic potential of curcumin in colorectal cancer ‒ A systematic review].
waves.study: systematic review dominated by mechanistic/preclinical evidence
waves.finding: Curcumin shows pro-apoptotic, anti-inflammatory, and chemosensitization mechanisms, with nanoformulations proposed to improve bioavailability.
waves.safety: Clinical efficacy and safety remain unvalidated; mechanistic evidence must not be presented as proven cancer treatment.

waves.title: Unraveling Riboflavin-Mediated Mitochondrial Modulation as a Therapeutic Pathway in Neurological Disorders: An Integrative Systematic Review.
waves.study: integrative systematic review of 23 studies; 7 clinical trials plus preclinical work
waves.finding: Riboflavin has plausible mitochondrial mechanisms and some human signals, with clearer clinical footing in selected migraine/stroke contexts; many other applications remain preclinical.
waves.safety: Mechanistic breadth should not be presented as broad neurologic efficacy.

waves.title: Autophagy activation in granulosa cells as a mechanism of astaxanthin action: evidence from a pilot randomised trial in PMOS-associated infertility.
waves.study: triple-blind placebo-controlled pilot RCT; 50 enrolled, 44 completed
waves.population: women with PMOS-associated anovulatory infertility undergoing oocyte retrieval
waves.finding: Astaxanthin altered granulosa-cell autophagy/apoptosis markers and improved adjusted mature-oocyte yield and selected embryo-quality measures; pregnancy outcomes were not significantly improved.
waves.safety: Pilot mechanistic/surrogate reproductive outcomes require larger replication before fertility claims.

waves.title: Effects of vitamin D supplementation on patients with systemic lupus erythematosus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Vitamin D increased 25(OH)D and reduced pooled disease-activity scores with some complement improvements, while ESR, fatigue, and several antibody outcomes were not consistently improved.
waves.safety: Adjunctive autoimmune-disease evidence is outcome-specific and requires higher-quality trials.

waves.title: Best Evidence Summary of Folic Acid Supplementation for Prevention of Neural Tube Defects in Women of Childbearing Age.
waves.finding: The evidence base strongly supports preconception and first-trimester folic-acid supplementation for neural-tube-defect prevention, with risk-stratified clinical recommendations.
waves.safety: Dose depends on risk and clinical context; high-risk dosing should not be generalized to everyone.

waves.title: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic potential of quercetin in ovarian functions.
waves.population: ovarian-aging, PCOS, ovarian-insufficiency, and ovarian-damage literature
waves.finding: Quercetin demonstrates antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and endocrine mechanisms across ovarian-condition models.
waves.safety: Evidence is predominantly mechanistic/preclinical and does not establish long-term human reproductive efficacy or dosing.

waves.title: Ginseng Berry Concentrate Alleviates Fatigue in Humans: A Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Double-Blinded Clinical Trial.
waves.finding: A proprietary ginseng-berry concentrate improved selected fatigue measures and resting lactate versus placebo; broader benefit strengthened in a post-hoc subgroup.
waves.safety: Small product-specific trial and post-hoc subgroup findings require replication before generalizing to ginseng products.

waves.title: Influence of melatonin supplementation on cancer-related fatigue: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
waves.finding: Melatonin produced a small pooled improvement in cancer-related fatigue, with benefit concentrated in longer-duration trials.
waves.safety: Small effect and oncology context limit generalization; duration subgrouping is not a dosing prescription.

waves.title: Collagen-ORC Versus Standard Treatment in Diabetic Foot Ulcers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomised Trials.
waves.study: systematic review of 6 studies; focused pooled analysis of 2 collagen-combination RCTs
waves.finding: Collagen-combination dressings increased complete wound closure versus control in a small pooled analysis, with other studies showing signals for wound-area reduction.
waves.safety: This is local wound-dressing evidence—not oral collagen-supplement evidence—and certainty is limited by small heterogeneous trials.

waves.title: Effect of omega-3 supplementation vs. placebo on blood lipid levels in patients with ischemic heart disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
waves.finding: Omega-3 supplementation reduced triglycerides and LDL-C; total cholesterol showed a borderline reduction and HDL-C rose only after sensitivity analysis.
waves.safety: Lipid changes in secondary prevention are not equivalent to demonstrated cardiovascular-event reduction.

waves.title: Cognitive Benefits of Ginseng: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Changes in Mini-Mental State Examination and Alzheimer's Disease Assessment Scale-Cognitive Subscale Scores.
waves.population: people with memory impairment, MCI, or Alzheimer disease
waves.finding: Ginseng produced small improvements on MMSE and ADAS-Cog pooled measures.
waves.safety: Limited trials and uncertain long-term effects prevent strong cognitive-treatment claims.

waves.title: Effects of Caffeine Supplementation on Exercise Performance in Volleyball Players: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.study: systematic review/meta-analysis of 11 blinded crossover studies
waves.finding: Acute caffeine improved several volleyball-specific actions and small-to-moderate measures of jump, grip, and agility performance.
waves.safety: Sport-specific acute ergogenic evidence does not establish universal dosing or safety.

waves.title: Association Between Dietary Calcium or Dairy Product Intake and Metabolic Syndrome Risk: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
waves.finding: Higher dietary calcium and dairy intake were associated with lower metabolic-syndrome prevalence and more favorable component profiles.
waves.safety: Cross-sectional associations cannot establish causality or calcium-supplement prevention benefit.

waves.title: Effect of Probiotic Supplementation on Cariogenic Streptococcus mutans Levels: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
waves.population: human participants assessed for cariogenic Streptococcus mutans
waves.finding: Most probiotic interventions produced only small, transient reductions in S. mutans without a consistent significant advantage over placebo.
waves.safety: Strain-specific microbiological shifts did not consistently translate to clinical caries outcomes.

waves.title: Effects of Synbiotic Supplementation on Blood and Urinary Concentrations of Factors Related to Kidney Stone Formation in Overweight or Obese Patients with Hyperoxaluria: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
waves.population: overweight or obese patients with hyperoxaluria
waves.finding: Synbiotic supplementation significantly reduced urinary oxalate versus baseline and placebo, while other measured blood and urinary stone-risk parameters did not significantly change.
waves.safety: Small trial and surrogate urinary outcome do not establish prevention of clinical kidney stones.

waves.title: Development and Validation of Questionnaires for Quantifying Intake from Dietary Supplements: A Scoping Review.
waves.study: scoping review of 15 supplement-intake questionnaires; 13 validated
waves.finding: Questionnaires showed format- and nutrient-dependent measurement error, often overestimating intake; correlations with reference methods were generally moderate-to-high but especially poor for iron.
waves.safety: This is evidence-quality infrastructure: supplement exposure estimates can be biased by instrument design and incomplete development reporting.

waves.title: Evaluating probiotic monotherapy in Helicobacter pylori infection: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials with trial sequential analysis.
waves.study: meta-analysis of 28 RCTs with trial-sequential analysis
waves.population: people with H. pylori infection receiving probiotic monotherapy without antibiotics
waves.finding: Probiotics reduced H. pylori colonization/bacterial load and modestly improved GI symptoms, but complete eradication was only 16.8%; L. reuteri showed the strongest strain-specific signal.
waves.safety: Probiotic monotherapy should not be represented as an effective replacement for eradication therapy; evidence supports at most a limited supportive role.
